paragraphs: Answering a question about a document is more useful when a model can also identify the page region supporting its answer. This paper addresses cases where that evidence is very small or surrounded by complicated content. The authors argue that locating evidence in a single step often produces imprecise boundaries or confuses relevant and irrelevant material.

Their method refines evidence locations progressively. It represents localization using probability distributions and formulates their movement toward the evidence as an optimal transport problem. Wasserstein gradient flow supplies the theoretical description of this refinement. Because the continuous process is impractical to compute directly, the method uses the Jordan–Kinderlehrer–Otto scheme to turn it into discrete optimization steps.

The authors then derive a loss that makes this formulation trainable within a neural network, connecting the mathematical construction to coarse-to-fine localization. Experiments report significant improvements in both finding evidence and generating answers. These findings support progressive localization as a way to improve the supporting evidence and the resulting response together.
icml-2026-a-progressive-evidence-localiz.tldr: Progressive evidence refinement using optimal transport improves document evidence localization and answer generation in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: When only a few questions can be asked, each question should help reveal something useful about the respondent. This paper studies adaptive questioning for predicting unasked responses and user-dependent indicators. It targets settings where users differ substantially, the information space is large, or little is initially known about a new user.

The proposed model represents uncertainty about a user through a finite collection of AI personas. Each persona supplies response probabilities generated by a language model. As the user answers questions, the system updates the probabilities associated with those personas. This construction allows closed-form posterior updates and predictions formed by mixing the persona-specific response distributions.

Those efficient updates support sequential question selection through Bayesian design: observations inform which question to ask next. Experiments on synthetic data and WorldValuesBench report accurate probabilistic predictions and an interpretable elicitation process. The finite persona dictionary is central to the approach, supplying both its expressive starting assumptions about users and its computationally manageable representation of uncertainty.
icml-2026-adaptive-querying-with-ai-pers.tldr: A finite dictionary of language-model-generated personas enables efficient Bayesian question selection and accurate user-response predictions.

paragraphs: Agents that use tools need environments where they can practice sequences of actions and observe the consequences. The paper identifies a shortage of diverse, reliable environments as a barrier to scaling this training. Agent World Model addresses that shortage with a fully synthetic generation pipeline producing 1,000 environments covering everyday scenarios.

The environments run on code and databases, with tools through which agents interact. This gives state changes an executable foundation and, according to the authors, makes them more reliable and consistent than environments simulated by language models. The authors also report more efficient interaction than collecting trajectories from realistic environments. Accessible database states help define reliable rewards for training.

The paper uses these environments for large-scale reinforcement learning of agents that perform multiple rounds of tool use. Across three benchmarks, training exclusively in synthetic environments produces strong generalization beyond the training distribution. The result supports executable synthetic environments as a useful training resource without requiring environments tailored to each evaluation benchmark.
icml-2026-agent-world-model-infinity-syn.tldr: Training tool-using agents in 1,000 executable synthetic environments yields strong generalization across three benchmarks.

paragraphs: A vision-language model can answer incorrectly because it misread the image or because it reasoned poorly about what it saw. The authors argue that failing to distinguish these causes creates a credit-assignment problem during training. It can contribute to a seesaw effect in which improvements to perception and reasoning fail to arrive together.

Their reinforcement learning framework explicitly interleaves perception steps with reasoning steps, making perception available for targeted supervision. Perception Verification uses a proxy described as blindfolded reasoning to reward perceptual fidelity independently of the final reasoning outcome. This separates the assessment of visual information from whether the complete solution ultimately succeeds.

For free-form vision-language tasks, Structured Verbal Verification replaces variable language-model judgments with structured algorithmic execution. A Modality-Aware Credit Assignment mechanism combines these techniques and directs rewards toward the relevant source of error. The abstract reports simultaneous gains across a broad range of tasks using a single model, supporting more specific training feedback as a route to better perception and reasoning together.
icml-2026-bad-seeing-or-bad-thinking-rew.tldr: Separately verifying perception and routing rewards by error source helps a single vision-language model improve perception and reasoning together.

paragraphs: Removing selected information from a pretrained multimodal model is difficult because knowledge within each modality interacts with knowledge shared across modalities. A change intended to forget particular data can therefore affect other knowledge. This paper seeks more effective and reliable forgetting while keeping its effects localized to the intended information.

The authors introduce a causal perspective that separates knowledge into components. Their Multimodal Variational Inference method infers factors specific to individual modalities and factors consistent across them, even with incomplete sample observations. This provides a finer representation of what a multimodal example contains than treating the whole example as a single forgetting target.

The method then applies contrastive semantic editing to regulate forgetting using those separated components. Experiments in privacy-sensitive and copyright-sensitive scenarios report effective unlearning while maintaining high reliability and locality. The stated contribution is a more targeted way to manage interconnected multimodal knowledge, with the reported evidence supporting preservation of unrelated information alongside the desired forgetting.
icml-2026-beyond-sample-level-forgetting.tldr: Separating modality-specific and shared knowledge enables more targeted multimodal unlearning with reported gains in reliability and locality.

paragraphs: This paper treats reasoning as a problem of selecting actions based on their projected future consequences. Its architectural contribution is a Test-Time Control layer that places planning inside a language model. The layer operates over latent states during inference, allowing an internal planning computation to inform the model before it produces a prediction.

The planning mechanism uses a finite-horizon linear quadratic regulator, or LQR, together with a value function represented within the architecture. That value function supplies a nested optimization objective. To make the computation practical, the authors derive a solver using a symplectic formulation and implement it as a fused CUDA kernel supporting parallel execution with minimal overhead.

Integrated into pretrained language models as adapters, the layers improve mathematical reasoning in the reported evaluations. The abstract reports gains of up to +27.8% on MATH-500 and two- to threefold Pass@8 improvements on AMC and AIME. These results support latent-state optimal control as an effective architectural mechanism for reasoning in the tested settings.
icml-2026-beyond-test-time-memory-state-.tldr: Test-Time Control layers embed efficient latent-state planning into pretrained language models and improve mathematical reasoning in reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for language models involves large data transfers and complicated dependencies between computations. The authors identify a scaling bottleneck in frameworks where one node dispatches both instructions and data. As training grows, that shared center can constrain communication and reduce the benefit of adding more hardware.

DistFlow distributes these responsibilities across multiple controllers and separates data movement from control decisions. Its decentralized Data Coordinator accounts for the training system's parallelism and uses local caching, load balancing, and asynchronous double buffering. These mechanisms aim to reduce communication overhead and limit delays caused by slower participants. A scheduler organized as a directed acyclic graph supports fine-grained execution of independent tasks.

Experiments show near-linear scaling up to 512 GPUs and throughput improvements of up to 2.63 times over state-of-the-art frameworks. These are system-efficiency findings: they indicate that the architecture can carry out more training work at scale. The central contribution is coordinating data and execution without routing both through a single dispatch point.
icml-2026-distflow-a-fully-distributed-r.tldr: DistFlow separates distributed data movement from task control, achieving near-linear scaling to 512 GPUs and up to 2.63-fold higher throughput.

paragraphs: Multimodal search agents can stop interacting before they have explored enough to solve a task well. The authors identify two contributing problems: rewards concentrated at the end fail to distinguish useful exploratory behavior, and redundant context makes feedback harder to absorb. DR-MMSearchAgent changes training signals to address both issues.

The framework uses structural proximity among complete trajectories within a training batch to derive advantage signals. This encourages trajectories of different lengths, including cases where they reach the same correct answer. Differentiated Gaussian rewards dynamically adjust tolerance for interaction, with the stated goals of maintaining information reliability and reducing redundant material.

The authors also construct a training dataset containing 3,602 question-answer pairs, each requiring at least three reasoning steps. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance, including an 8.4% improvement over MMSearch-R1 on FVQA-test. The results support rewarding the structure of exploration alongside answer correctness, while managing the amount of information accumulated during multi-turn search.
icml-2026-dr-mmsearchagent-deepening-rea.tldr: DR-MMSearchAgent changes trajectory-level rewards to encourage useful exploration and reduce redundancy, improving reported multimodal search performance.

paragraphs: Examples placed in a prompt can strongly affect a language model's answer, but testing many candidate example sets requires expensive model calls. This paper proposes judging whether a particular query and context will work as a more economical basis for selection. Its DiSP framework samples possible contexts and predicts their suitability.

During training, random demonstration trials estimate how often each query succeeds. A lightweight router learns to predict query difficulty, and separate judges learn to score contexts for different difficulty levels. At inference, the system evaluates sampled contexts within an explicit budget and stops when one is accepted. It typically makes a single language-model call and emits diagnostic risk tags when no suitable context is found.

Across five classification datasets using Llama 3–8B and Qwen 2.5–7B, DiSP achieves the best average accuracy. Reported improvements reach 3.4% over strong learned selection baselines, with up to 23-fold end-to-end speedup. The findings support spending inexpensive judgment computation on context selection before invoking the larger model.
icml-2026-easier-to-judge-than-to-find-p.tldr: DiSP uses difficulty-specific judges to select prompt examples efficiently, improving classification accuracy while typically requiring one language-model call.

paragraphs: Interpreting EEG signals requires modeling patterns across time and relationships across brain locations. The paper also identifies a gap between these physiological measurements and the higher-level language used to describe them. KAST-BAR aims to connect both forms of information within a foundation model for neural decoding across tasks.

A Dual-Stream Hierarchical Attention encoder combines local temporal dynamics with global spatial context to represent the brain's complex topology. A Knowledge-Anchored Semantic Profiler then synthesizes textual profiles grounded in physiology and specific to individual instances. Those profiles guide a Semantic Text-Aware Refiner, which uses Latent Expert Queries to dynamically reconstruct the EEG representations.

The authors pretrain the model on 21 diverse datasets, incorporating expert medical knowledge into its signal representations. They report state-of-the-art results across six downstream tasks. The findings support combining structured spatiotemporal modeling with instance-specific semantic guidance: the text-derived knowledge participates in refining the physiological representation itself, linking the two sources of information within the model.
icml-2026-kast-bar-knowledge-anchored-se.tldr: KAST-BAR combines EEG topology modeling with expert semantic guidance and reports state-of-the-art performance across six downstream tasks.

paragraphs: An assistant watching first-person video needs to remember where objects were and interpret those locations as its user moves. This paper introduces UCS-Bench to evaluate that combination of spatial reasoning, long-term memory, and alignment with the user's current position. The dataset contains more than 170 hours of observations and over 8,100 timestamped questions.

The proposed DirectMe framework incrementally builds and maintains structured spatial memory from incoming video. It connects visual perception to memory updates and spatial reasoning, supporting object tracking and later recall relative to the user's movement. This is designed for questions that span long periods, revisit earlier interactions, or involve ambiguity caused by changes in viewpoint.

Experiments report significant improvements in the spatial reasoning of leading multimodal language models. DirectMe also outperforms many spatially aware models and models for long streaming videos. These results support explicitly maintained spatial memory as a useful component for assistants that must reason about changing scenes and past observations from a moving user's perspective.
icml-2026-keep-it-in-mind-user-centric-c.tldr: UCS-Bench evaluates continual spatial reasoning from first-person video, and DirectMe improves performance using incrementally updated spatial memory.

paragraphs: An agent may make several correct decisions before a later mistake causes the entire task to fail. Training from that final outcome can penalize useful early behavior and discard learning opportunities from partially successful attempts. This paper identifies those credit-assignment and sample-efficiency problems as obstacles for language agents facing long sequences of decisions.

BEACON uses the compositional structure of tasks to divide trajectories at milestones. Within each segment, temporal reward shaping gives credit for partial progress. Advantage estimates at two scales help evaluate local actions without letting distant failures dominate their assessment. Milestones therefore provide intermediate boundaries for deciding which parts of a trajectory deserve reinforcement.

BEACON consistently outperforms GRPO and GiGPO on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld. On long-horizon ALFWorld tasks, it reaches a 92.9% success rate versus GRPO's 53.5%, while effective sample utilization increases from 23.7% to 82.0%. These results indicate that milestone-based feedback can extract substantially more useful training signal from the trajectories agents already generate.
icml-2026-milestone-guided-policy-learni.tldr: BEACON credits progress between task milestones, improving long-horizon agent success and effective use of training trajectories.

paragraphs: Clustering can supply useful features for prediction, but choosing one clustering resolution fixes how broadly or narrowly all samples are grouped. This paper builds on the observation that changing resolution produces a finite set of structurally stable partitions, called configurations. It asks whether a predictor can learn which configurations matter for each individual sample.

The proposed Configuration-Mixed Prediction setting allows sample-dependent weighting of those partitions. MixConfig implements this idea as a feature augmentation module that extracts configurations from an embedding. Its selector combines sample context, cluster membership, and stability statistics to learn energy-aware mixing weights. The resulting features can be used with different predictor architectures.

Experiments across tabular, molecular, vision, and text tasks report consistent improvements over fixed-resolution and static baselines. Gains are particularly pronounced when training data are scarce. The findings suggest that multiple stable views of an embedding contain complementary predictive information, and that adapting their contribution per sample can be more useful than making one global resolution choice.
icml-2026-mixing-configurations-for-down.tldr: MixConfig learns sample-specific mixtures of stable clustering configurations, improving prediction across domains, especially with limited training data.

paragraphs: Entropy measures the diversity of a language model's possible outputs and helps characterize its exploration during reinforcement fine-tuning. Although training methods increasingly monitor or adjust entropy, the authors argue that its response to model updates needs a clearer theoretical account. This paper develops an analysis of how those updates change entropy.

The analysis starts with a discriminant expression for the entropy change caused by a single logit update. From that foundation, the authors derive a first-order expression and extend it to Group Relative Policy Optimization. This links changes in the model's output scores to the direction of entropy change during a specific reinforcement learning update.

The resulting insights motivate entropy-discriminator clipping methods and offer a common interpretation of several existing entropy-based techniques. Empirical results support the main analytical conclusions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the derived methods. The contribution combines an account of training dynamics with practical controls for balancing exploration and exploitation, while retaining the first-order nature of the relevant expression.
icml-2026-on-the-entropy-dynamics-in-rei.tldr: A theoretical analysis of entropy changes during reinforcement fine-tuning motivates effective clipping methods for controlling output diversity.

paragraphs: Alignment can improve language-model output quality while making different generations more alike. This is especially consequential for open-ended tasks, where varied responses are valuable. Base-Aligned Model Collaboration addresses the trade-off by combining a base model and its aligned counterpart during generation, allowing both to contribute to the same response.

BACo makes a routing decision at each token using uncertainty and content-based signals. The router determines which model supplies the next token. The paper develops several routing strategies, offering control over the balance between diversity and quality. The method operates at inference time within a single generation pass, without requiring another post-training stage.

Evaluations cover three open-ended generation tasks and 13 diversity and quality metrics. BACo consistently outperforms state-of-the-art inference-time baselines, with the best router producing a reported 21.3% joint improvement in diversity and quality. Human evaluations also support the result. The evidence suggests that token-level collaboration can preserve useful variation while retaining the benefits of alignment.
icml-2026-optimizing-diversity-and-quali.tldr: BACo routes generation between base and aligned models token by token to improve output diversity and quality together.

paragraphs: Realistic AI image edits can evade forgery detectors that depend on physical imaging noise absent from synthetic content. This paper instead examines a statistical trace associated with diffusion generation. The authors theoretically show that diffusion suppresses local high-frequency variance, producing an energy difference distinguishable from the natural entropy of optical imaging.

FLAME uses a LAD map to expose these anomalies and combines it with a parameter-efficient adapter for SAM. Together, these components identify manipulated regions at pixel level. The approach connects the proposed statistical signal to spatial localization, so the output indicates where a forgery occurs within an image.

The paper also introduces EditStream, an automated pipeline that continuously synthesizes instruction-based training examples to help keep forensic data aligned with evolving editing models. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on AI-generated forgery datasets, significant improvements over previous methods, and generalization to unseen generative architectures. These findings support the usefulness of diffusion-related energy anomalies across the evaluated forgery settings.
icml-2026-order-within-chaos-capturing-i.tldr: FLAME localizes AI image edits using diffusion-related energy anomalies and reports strong performance on unseen generative architectures.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning depends on the quality of both its training environment and the signals used to judge behavior. RLAnything treats these as components that can improve alongside the policy. Its framework links policy training, reward-model training, and environment adaptation in a feedback loop intended to strengthen the overall learning process.

The policy receives feedback on individual steps as well as final outcomes. The reward model is jointly optimized using consistency feedback, and its improvements feed back into policy training. An automatic environment adaptation mechanism uses critic feedback from both models to improve their training conditions. The abstract describes this adaptation as motivated by theory.

Empirically, each additional component consistently improves the system. The paper reports gains of 8.5% for Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking on OSWorld and 21.2% and 12.1% for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on AlfWorld and LiveBench, respectively. These results support coordinating improvements across the environment, evaluator, and acting model instead of treating the learning signal as fixed throughout training.
icml-2026-rlanything-forge-environment-p.tldr: RLAnything jointly adapts the policy, reward model, and environment, producing reported gains across three practical evaluation settings.

paragraphs: Concept erasure aims to suppress unsafe image content while preserving a generator's broader capabilities. This becomes difficult in next-scale autoregressive generation because early scales compress semantic information tightly. Unsafe concepts can be entangled with unrelated content, making broad interventions liable to alter more of the image than intended.

ScaleErasure operates during inference and selects the predicted logits most relevant to the unsafe concept. It runs two additional forward passes, one conditioned on that concept and one on a corresponding safe concept. Their outputs guide selected logits away from the unsafe concept and toward the safe one. Selection and guidance span scales, tokens, and bit channels.

This targeted intervention is designed to address semantic entanglement while limiting disruption to other content. Experiments show more precise concept erasure than adapted baselines for next-scale autoregressive models, with general generative capability largely preserved. The reported result supports selective inference-time guidance, while the two additional forward passes are an explicit part of the method's computation.
icml-2026-scaleerasure-inference-time-mi.tldr: ScaleErasure selectively guides image-generation logits away from unsafe concepts while largely preserving general generative capability.

paragraphs: Proving system software correct can require reasoning about complicated heap manipulation. Even when engineers provide correct specifications, such as loop invariants, automated solvers can fail to prove the remaining separation-logic conditions. This paper introduces SL-VC to measure that difficulty, with 289 verification conditions drawn from textbook algorithms and real C software.

The benchmark includes code from the LiteOS linked-list library and mini-gmp. Evaluations show that general-purpose language models and existing language-model-based Rocq provers struggle with these conditions. The authors respond with SPLIT, a framework whose tactic library makes proof-state changes more predictable for a language model.

SPLIT organizes proof construction into two stages that separate spatial reasoning from pure reasoning, matching the structure of separation logic. Experiments on SL-VC show consistent improvements over existing approaches. The results suggest that specialized proof operations and a workflow aligned with the logic can make language-model-assisted proof synthesis more effective for the evaluated system-software verification problems.
icml-2026-sl-vc-a-benchmark-and-automate.tldr: SL-VC exposes difficulties in separation-logic proof synthesis, while SPLIT improves results through specialized tactics and staged reasoning.

paragraphs: Vision-language-action models can run faster by removing computation on visual tokens judged unimportant. However, decisions based only on the current action can discard useful context. This paper uses the observation that images from consecutive action steps are highly similar to motivate token selection informed by both current information and model history.

SpecPrune-VLA performs pruning at two levels without additional training. At the action level, it combines global history and local attention to reduce visual tokens. Within the model, it adjusts pruning layer by layer according to token importance. A lightweight controller uses end-effector speed to classify actions as coarse or fine and changes pruning aggressiveness accordingly.

Experiments report speedups of up to 1.57 times in LIBERO simulation and 1.70 times on real-world tasks, with negligible degradation in success rate. These results support adapting computational savings to both temporal context and action characteristics. The reported maximum speedups describe the evaluated settings, while the method's central mechanism is selective computation at multiple levels.
icml-2026-specprune-vla-accelerating-vis.tldr: SpecPrune-VLA combines action history, layer importance, and motion-aware control to accelerate inference with negligible reported success-rate degradation.

paragraphs: An agent learning in a changing environment needs an exploration level that responds to those changes. A fixed entropy setting can encourage excessive exploration during stable periods and insufficient exploration after a shift. This paper asks how the strength of exploration should scale with the amount of environmental drift.

Under standard assumptions, the authors formulate entropy scheduling as a dynamic-regret trade-off between following a changing comparator and keeping updates stable. Their analysis yields a square-root scaling rule relating entropy weight to an online proxy for non-stationarity. That proxy may be conservative, so the rule does not require it to measure drift exactly.

Adaptive Entropy Scheduling implements the idea by adjusting the entropy coefficient or temperature during training using observable drift signals. It requires almost no structural changes and adds minimal overhead. Across four algorithm variants, 12 tasks, and four drift modes, it significantly reduces drift-related performance degradation and speeds recovery after abrupt changes, supporting adaptive exploration in the tested non-stationary settings.
icml-2026-tracking-drift-variation-aware.tldr: Adaptive Entropy Scheduling uses observable drift signals to adjust exploration, reducing performance losses and accelerating recovery after environmental changes.

paragraphs: Clicks, copies, and skips offer abundant feedback about language-model responses without requiring explicit ratings. However, learning preferences from those actions is difficult: the absence of a positive action does not establish a negative judgment. Responses also differ in their likelihood of attracting feedback, creating selection bias in the observations.

ImplicitRM addresses both issues through a model that stratifies training samples into four latent groups. Using that structure, the authors derive a likelihood-maximization objective described as theoretically unbiased. The method therefore accounts for hidden distinctions in the feedback-generating process instead of applying ordinary positive-negative classification directly to observed interactions.

Experiments across multiple language-model backbones and benchmark datasets show accurate reward modeling from implicit feedback and improved downstream reinforcement learning from human feedback. The findings support using naturally occurring user actions as a scalable training signal when their ambiguity and selection effects are modeled explicitly. The theoretical unbiasedness claim concerns the proposed objective, while the experiments establish its reported practical usefulness.
icml-2026-unbiased-reward-modeling-from-.tldr: ImplicitRM models hidden feedback groups to address missing negatives and selection bias when learning rewards from user interactions.

paragraphs: This paper studies variable clustering: grouping variables using a multi-factor block model. Its central contribution connects that modeling problem to regularized subspace clustering through a distributionally robust form of nodewise regression. The connection gives the authors an optimization-based route for estimating the variable groups within the stated model.

The robust formulation includes a region whose size must be chosen. The authors provide a data-driven way to select that size, making this choice part of the proposed procedure. They also derive a convex relaxation of the optimization problem and develop an implementation based on ADMM. These contributions link the statistical formulation to a computational method intended to run efficiently.

Extensive numerical studies validate the method, and the abstract reports superior performance. The stated evidence concerns the proposed method within those numerical evaluations. The paper's contribution combines a modeling connection, a procedure for selecting the robust-region size, and an optimization algorithm, bringing the theoretical formulation and its practical implementation into one approach.
icml-2026-variable-clustering-via-distri.tldr: A distributionally robust nodewise-regression formulation connects variable clustering to subspace clustering and supports an efficient optimization procedure.

paragraphs: Interactive video world models must generate plausible scenes while following interaction signals over extended sequences. WorldCompass introduces reinforcement learning after initial training to improve both properties. Its design focuses on the autoregressive video setting, where generated clips become part of a continuing sequence that the interaction signals are meant to steer.

The framework generates and evaluates multiple candidate samples at a single target clip. This clip-level rollout strategy provides more localized reward feedback while improving rollout efficiency. Complementary rewards assess interaction-following accuracy and visual quality, giving direct supervision on both objectives and helping suppress reward hacking. A negative-aware fine-tuning strategy and additional optimizations support efficient learning.

Evaluations apply WorldCompass to the open-source WorldPlay model and report significant improvements in interaction accuracy and visual fidelity across several scenarios. The results support evaluating alternatives at the clip level and rewarding both controllability and appearance together. The demonstrated gains concern the tested model and scenarios, establishing the practical value of the proposed post-training framework there.
icml-2026-worldcompass-reinforcement-lea.tldr: WorldCompass improves interactive video generation through clip-level reinforcement learning with complementary rewards for interaction accuracy and visual quality.

paragraphs: A travel plan can fail because one early choice makes later requirements impossible to satisfy. WorldTravel evaluates this interdependence using 150 real-world scenarios across five cities, each requiring an average of more than 15 linked temporal and logical constraints. It targets planning problems where individually reasonable local choices may not produce a feasible complete itinerary.

WorldTravel-Webscape adds the challenge of finding those requirements in realistic interfaces. Its more than 2,000 rendered webpages preserve dense information and layout-dependent presentation. Agents must extract usable constraints from what they see and then coordinate those constraints into an executable plan, combining information acquisition with extended planning.

An evaluation of 10 frontier models reveals severe difficulties. GPT-5.2 achieves 28.0% feasibility with text-only inputs and 3.4% in the multimodal environment. The authors also observe a planning-reliability collapse around 10 constraints. These benchmark findings suggest that extracting constraints from webpages and maintaining consistency across many dependent decisions are complementary bottlenecks; the observed threshold describes the evaluated setting.
icml-2026-worldtravel-a-realistic-multim.tldr: WorldTravel shows that agents struggle to produce feasible travel plans when constraints are tightly linked and must be extracted from rendered webpages.
